paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.English: The plot titled “Errors (COPA)” illustrates how an error metric varies with adapter rank for the COPA dataset, showing a single series with uncertainty bars. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and uses a linear scale with four discrete tick values at 4, 16, 64, and 256 (no units shown). The y-axis has no explicit label in the figure, uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 0.0 up to about 0.75, with major tick labels shown at 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6. One line is displayed as a solid black line connecting large green circular markers, with black vertical error bars at each marker. The series starts at rank 4 with a y-value around 0.18, decreases slightly at rank 16 to around 0.15, then rises sharply at rank 64 to around 0.41, and remains at a similar level at rank 256 around 0.42; the error bars are shortest around rank 64 and visibly larger at ranks 4 and 256, extending roughly on the order of a few hundredths to about a tenth of a unit in y.
model_annotations.German: The plot titled “Errors (COPA)” illustrates how an error metric varies with adapter rank for the COPA setting, with uncertainty shown via vertical error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and shows four discrete tick labels (4, 16, 64, 256) that are evenly spaced along the axis (scale type not explicitly indicated), spanning from 4 to 256. The y-axis has no explicit label, uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 at the bottom to about 0.8 at the top, with major tick labels at 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6 (regular interval of 0.3). A single solid black line connects green filled circular markers at each rank, and each marker has a black vertical error bar with caps. The series starts at rank 4 near 0.18, dips slightly at rank 16 near 0.15, then increases to around 0.41 at rank 64, and remains at a similar level at rank 256 around 0.42; the error bars are smallest around rank 64 and largest at rank 256, with rank 256 spanning roughly from the mid-0.3s to just above 0.5.
